Record the top claims. Key suspicion: mantissa reduction — after halving mantissa, mantissa*0.5 can be less than 1? No: mantissa in [1,2), if >1.65 halved gives [0.825,1)? Wait mantissa in [1,2); if mantissa>1.65 then mantissa*0.5 in (0.825,1.0)! That gives z negative and |z| up to (1-0.825)/(1.825)≈0.096, fine. But wait: mantissa*0.5 gives values <1, and log(mantissa) then negative — actually log(u) = exponent*ln2 + log(mantissa_halved), consistent. z range bounded ~0.245. Fine.

Main risks: coefficient rounding 0.33333 error ~3.33e-6 in 1/3 term → local_log error ~2*z*3.33e-6*z^2 ≈ 6.7e-6*z^3 ≈ 9.9e-7 at z=0.245... close to tolerance; combined with truncation z^9/9 ≈ 0.245^9/9 ≈ 3.1e-7*... 0.245^9 ≈ 1.1e-6, /9 ≈1.2e-7. Also note mantissa in [1,1.65) un-halved gives z up to (1.65-1)/(2.65)=0.2455; halved branch mantissa*0.5 ∈ (0.825,1.0] gives z negative. So max |z| ≈0.245. Coefficient error ~1e-6 near limit → claim it can exceed 1e-6. Also negative mantissa side: z negative down to -0.096 — fine.

Second claim: near x=-1 region — u ~4.88e-4, exponent=-11, mantissa ~1.95→halved to ~0.98... fine. Correction term: correction = (x-(u-1))/u. In FP32, u-1 = x exactly? For x<0, u=1+x, u-1 = x exactly (Sterbenz). Then correction = 0! Actually u-1 in FP32 rounds to x exactly since 0.5≤u≤2... for u in [0.5,2], Sterbenz holds, so u-1 exact, correction=0. For u>2 (x>1), u-1 ≠ x, correction nonzero. Hmm, but FP32 u = fl(1+x) already loses precision vs real 1+x when x>1 (x FP16 has 11 bits; 1+x with x in (1,2) loses low bit). E.g. x=1.5 → u=2.5 exact. x = 1.0625+...? FP16 values >1 have spacing 2^-10; 1+x in [2,4) representable exactly? u=fl(1+x): 1+x may not be representable in FP32? FP32 has 24 bits; 1+x for x in (1, 65504) — x has 11 significant bits, 1+x needs up to... x=65504: 1+65504=65505, representable in FP32 exactly (needs 17 bits). Generally 1+x with x FP16: x = m*2^e, 1+x requires up to ~ e+24 bits? x=65504: exponent 16, 65505 needs bits at 2^0, exponent 16 → 17 bits, fits. Actually any FP16 value plus 1: worst case x slightly above 2^k where k small... x in [1,2): 1+x in [2,4), x = 1+11 bits, 1+x needs bits down to 2^-10, range [2,4) → needs 12 bits. Always exact in FP32. So u exact, correction ~0 exactly? Not exactly: u-1 computed in FP32 is exact Sterbenz for u in [0.5,2]; for u>2, u-1 exact too (subtracting 1 from u with exponent ≥1... u-1 for u in [2,4): u has exponent 1, u-1 in [1,3) — Sterbenz doesn't apply but is it exact? u = 2^e*(1+f), u-1... for u∈[2,4), u-1 needs bits down to 2^-22 relative... u has 24-bit significand starting at bit position 1 (value in [2,4)), so lowest bit 2^-22; u-1 in [1,4) representable down to 2^-23. Generally exact when u's low bits ≤ representable. For u in [2,4), u-1 = 1 + (u-2), u-2 has bits down to 2^-22, representable exactly. Yes exact. So x - (u-1) = 0 exactly always (u=1+x exactly in FP32 for FP16 x). So correction = 0 identically — correction harmless, not a bug source. So main risk is just polynomial accuracy. Errors: coefficient errors give local_log error ≈ 2z*(Δc3 z^2 + Δc5 z^4 + Δc7 z^6) plus truncation 2z*(z^8/9 + ...). Δc3 = 1/3-0.33333 = 3.33e-6, Δc5 = 1/5-0.2 = ... 0.2 in float ≈ 0.20000000298? Wait 0.2 decimal vs 1/5 = 0.2 exactly equal in decimal; as FP32, 0.2 rounds—both same. 0.142857 vs 1/7=0.142857142857: Δ=1.43e-7. So error ≈ 2z*(3.33e-6 z² + 1.43e-7 z⁴) + truncation 2z*(z⁸/9·... truncation after z^7: true atanh = z + z³/3+z⁵/5+z⁷/7+z⁹/9+...; local_log = 2z*P(z²), P missing z⁸/9+...; error ≈ 2z*z⁸/9 = 2z⁹/9. At z=0.245: z⁹≈1.1e-6, so 2.5e-7. Coefficient: 2*0.245*3.33e-6*0.06 ≈ 9.8e-7. Total ≈1.2e-6 — right at/over 1e-6 tolerance! Strong candidate for a real failure near max z (mantissa near 1.65). That's claim 1.

Claim 2: FP32 rounding in intermediate: exponent.to(float32)*ln2_high — for exponent=16, high*16 rounding ~ulp(11)≈1e-6 already; final result magnitude 11, single FP32 rounding ulp = 2^-20*8 ≈ 9.5e-7... rounding error in final store alone can be ~ulp(11.09)/2 ≈ 4.8e-7.
